packet.headline_seed: Despite ‘misgivings,’ judge approves Elon Musk’s $1.5 million SEC settlement
packet.description_seed: The saga of Musk's tussle with the SEC over how he disclosed his growing stake in Twitter (now called X) has come to an end.

what: Despite ‘misgivings,’ judge approves Elon Musk’s $1.5 million SEC settlement

clean_source_blocks.text: Published by Global Banking & Finance Review July 8 (Reuters) - A federal judge on Wednesday approved the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission's settlement with Elon Musk over his purchase of Twitter shares, despite expressing "significant misgivings" about the "red flags" the accord raised. U.S. District Judge Sparkle Sooknanan in Washington, D.C., said she had only a limited role in assessing whether the settlement meets minimum standards of fairness and reasonableness, or instead "makes a mockery of judicial power," and questioned whether the Trump administration let the world's richest person off too easily.

See more of our coverage in your search results. A federal judge on Wednesday approved the Securities and Exchange Commission’s settlement with Elon Musk over his purchase of Twitter shares, despite expressing “significant misgivings” about the “red flags” the accord raised. US District Judge Sparkle Sooknanan in Washington, DC., said she had only a limited role in assessing whether the settlement meets minimum standards of fairness and reasonableness, or instead “makes a mockery of judicial power,” and questioned whether the Trump administration let the world’s richest person off too easily.

The Trump administration is letting Elon Musk pay a $1.5 million fine to settle a lawsuit that originally sought at least $150 million. If approved by a federal court, the proposed settlement submitted yesterday would require a trust in Musk’s name to pay a $1.5 million civil penalty to the government. The January 2025 lawsuit, filed in the last days of the Biden administration, relates to how Musk purchased a 9 percent stake in Twitter in 2022 and failed to disclose it within 10 days as required under US law. The Securities and Exchange Commission alleged that “Musk was able to continue purchasing shares at artificially low prices, allowing him to underpay by at least $150 million for shares he purchased after his beneficial ownership report was due.”

“A court presented with a consent judgment is not a rubber stamp. But neither is it an ombudsman,” Sooknanan wrote. “Whether the Executive Branch (through the SEC) has done enough to hold Mr. Musk to account for his alleged violation is, like many other issues, for our citizenry to decide at the ballot box.” Musk is a former adviser to Republican President Trump. Sooknanan was appointed to the bench by former Democratic President Joe Biden. An SEC spokesperson declined to comment. Musk’s lawyers did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The settlement requires a trust in Musk’s name to pay $1.5 million to resolve SEC claims that Musk took 11 days too long in March and April 2022 to disclose his early purchases of Twitter shares.

payload.title: Tuomari hyväksyi Elon Muskin 1,5 miljoonan dollarin sovun SEC:n kanssa
payload.summary: Yhdysvaltalainen liittovaltion tuomari hyväksyi sovun, jolla Elon Muskin nimissä oleva trusti maksaa 1,5 miljoonan dollarin siviilisakon Twitter-osakkeiden ostojen myöhäisestä ilmoittamisesta.
payload.content:
Yhdysvaltalainen liittovaltion tuomari Sparkle Sooknanan on hyväksynyt arvopaperimarkkinavalvoja SEC:n ja Elon Muskin välisen sovun, joka koskee Muskin vuonna 2022 tekemiä Twitter-osakkeiden ostoja ja niiden ilmoittamista viranomaisille. Sovun mukaan Muskin nimissä oleva trusti maksaa Yhdysvaltain valtiolle 1,5 miljoonan dollarin siviilisakon.

## Riita koski Twitter-omistuksen ilmoittamista

SEC:n kanne liittyi siihen, miten Musk kasvatti omistustaan Twitterissä ennen yhtiön myöhempää ostoa. Viranomaisen mukaan Musk hankki vuonna 2022 noin yhdeksän prosentin osuuden Twitteristä, mutta ei ilmoittanut omistuksestaan Yhdysvaltain lain edellyttämässä kymmenen päivän määräajassa.

Viranomainen väitti, että myöhästynyt ilmoitus antoi Muskille mahdollisuuden jatkaa osakkeiden ostamista keinotekoisen matalilla hinnoilla. SEC:n mukaan hän maksoi vähintään 150 miljoonaa dollaria liian vähän osakkeista, jotka hän osti sen jälkeen, kun omistusta koskeva raportti olisi pitänyt tehdä. Tammikuussa 2025 nostettu kanne oli peräisin Bidenin hallinnon viimeisiltä päiviltä.

## Tuomari näki sovussa varoitusmerkkejä

Washingtonissa toimiva Sooknanan hyväksyi sovun, mutta kirjoitti suhtautuvansa siihen huomattavin varauksin. Hänen mukaansa sopimus nosti esiin varoitusmerkkejä, ja hän kyseenalaisti, päästikö Trumpin hallinto maailman rikkaimmaksi kuvattua Muskia liian helpolla.

Sooknanan kuitenkin korosti, että tuomioistuimen rooli sovintotuomion arvioinnissa on rajallinen. Hänen mukaansa tuomarin on arvioitava, täyttääkö sopimus oikeudenmukaisuuden ja kohtuullisuuden vähimmäisvaatimukset, eikä tuomioistuin ole hallinnon valvova asiamies.

Tuomari kirjoitti myös, että kysymys siitä, onko toimeenpanovalta SEC:n kautta tehnyt tarpeeksi Muskin saattamiseksi vastuuseen väitetystä rikkomuksesta, kuuluu viime kädessä kansalaisten arvioitavaksi vaaleissa. Musk on toiminut presidentti Donald Trumpin neuvonantajana, kun taas Sooknananin nimitti tuomariksi entinen presidentti Joe Biden.

SEC:n edustaja ei kommentoinut päätöstä. Muskin asianajajat eivät vastanneet välittömästi kommenttipyyntöihin. Hyväksytty sovinto päättää SEC:n ja Muskin välisen riidan siitä, miten nopeasti hänen olisi pitänyt ilmoittaa varhaisista Twitter-osakeostoistaan maaliskuussa ja huhtikuussa 2022.
summary_bullets: Liittovaltion tuomari hyväksyi Elon Muskin ja SEC:n 1,5 miljoonan dollarin sovun.
Riidassa oli kyse Twitter-osakkeiden ostojen myöhäisestä ilmoittamisesta vuonna 2022.
Tuomari ilmaisi päätöksessään varauksia mutta katsoi roolinsa sovun arvioinnissa rajalliseksi.
payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu paketissa olleisiin neljään lähdekatkelmaan. Keskeiset luvut ja väitteet on rajattu niihin: 1,5 miljoonan dollarin sakko, noin yhdeksän prosentin Twitter-omistus, ilmoitusviivästys ja SEC:n vähintään 150 miljoonan dollarin väite.

Published by Global Banking & Finance Review July 8 (Reuters) - A federal judge on Wednesday approved the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission's settlement with Elon Musk over his purchase of Twitter shares, despite expressing "significant misgivings" about the "red flags" the accord raised. U.S. District Judge Sparkle Sooknanan in Washington, D.C., said she had only a limited role in assessing whether the settlement meets minimum standards of fairness and reasonableness, or instead "makes a mockery of judicial power," and questioned whether the Trump administration let the world's richest person off too easily.

A federal judge on Wednesday approved the Securities and Exchange Commission’s settlement with Elon Musk over his purchase of Twitter shares, despite expressing “significant misgivings” about the “red flags” the accord raised. US District Judge Sparkle Sooknanan in Washington, DC., said she had only a limited role in assessing whether the settlement meets minimum standards of fairness and reasonableness, or instead “makes a mockery of judicial power,” and questioned whether the Trump administration let the world’s richest person off too easily.

The Trump administration is letting Elon Musk pay a $1.5 million fine to settle a lawsuit that originally sought at least $150 million. If approved by a federal court, the proposed settlement submitted yesterday would require a trust in Musk’s name to pay a $1.5 million civil penalty to the government. The January 2025 lawsuit, filed in the last days of the Biden administration, relates to how Musk purchased a 9 percent stake in Twitter in 2022 and failed to disclose it within 10 days as required under US law. The Securities and Exchange Commission alleged that “Musk was able to continue purchasing shares at artificially low prices, allowing him to underpay by at least $150 million for shares he purchased after his beneficial ownership report was due.”

“A court presented with a consent judgment is not a rubber stamp. But neither is it an ombudsman,” Sooknanan wrote. “Whether the Executive Branch (through the SEC) has done enough to hold Mr. Musk to account for his alleged violation is, like many other issues, for our citizenry to decide at the ballot box.” Musk is a former adviser to Republican President Trump. Sooknanan was appointed to the bench by former Democratic President Joe Biden. An SEC spokesperson declined to comment. Musk’s lawyers did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The settlement requires a trust in Musk’s name to pay $1.5 million to resolve SEC claims that Musk took 11 days too long in March and April 2022 to disclose his early purchases of Twitter shares.
